Making Japanese curry? 🍛  Don’t just chop everything into random sizes. The way you cut your vegetables actually matters, especially if you want them nicely cooked and not disappear in curry. 🥕 𝐂𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐨𝐭 → rangiri cut Cutting it into irregular rolling pieces gives you different surfaces while keeping the pieces relatively similar in size, so they cook evenly. 🥔 𝐏𝐨𝐭𝐚𝐭𝐨 → bite-size chunks Not too small, so they have enough structure to hold their shape while becoming tender. 🧅 𝐎𝐧𝐢𝐨𝐧 → wedges Keeping the onion in wedges allows it to soften and become sweet without completely disappearing into the curry. It’s a small step, but proper cutting makes a difference in cooking time, texture and how your curry comes together. Save this for the next time you make Japanese kare raisu 🍛🇯🇵 𝘑𝘢𝘱𝘢𝘯𝘦𝘴𝘦 𝘤𝘰𝘰𝘬𝘪𝘯𝘨, 𝘮𝘢𝘥𝘦 𝘦𝘢𝘴𝘪𝘦𝘳 𝘸𝘪𝘵𝘩 𝘛𝘩𝘦𝘳𝘮𝘰𝘮𝘪𝘹. 𝘐𝘧 𝘺𝘰𝘶’𝘳𝘦 𝘤𝘶𝘳𝘪𝘰𝘶𝘴 𝘢𝘣𝘰𝘶𝘵 𝘰𝘸𝘯𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘰𝘯𝘦, 𝘮𝘦𝘴𝘴𝘢𝘨𝘦 𝘮𝘦. Healthy, cooling, filling & gut-friendly breakfast! Probiotic-rich, packed with iron, calcium, fiber & essential nutrients—perfect for weight loss & digestion ❤️ Light, satisfying & ideal for all ages, especially in summer ✨ Recipe: 🌿 Mix 2 tbsp ragi flour with 1 cup water to make a smooth slurry. In a pan, heat 2 cups water. Once it starts boiling, add the slurry and cook on medium flame till it thickens. Keep stirring continuously to avoid lumps. Let it cool completely. 🌿 In a bowl, add 1 cup fresh curd, 2–3 cups water, salt to taste, ¼ cup finely chopped onion, and 2 tbsp coriander leaves. Add the cooled ragi porridge and mix well. 🌿 Prepare the tadka: heat 1 tsp oil or ghee, add ½ tsp cumin seeds + mustard seeds, grated ginger, green chili, curry leaves, and a pinch of hing. Pour over the kanji. Enjoy! #ragimillet #raagikanji  #guthealth #healthybreakfast #milletrecipes

Let’s make Ragi mudde  A popular dish from Karnataka that replaces rice in a South Indian meal. Although an acquired taste, this humble dish packs in a ton of nutrition and is great to sop up any curry. In 2 cups of water, mix 1/2 cup ragi flour. Mix and boil until it is a little thick. This thick porridge-y concoction is Ragi Ambali, another spectacular dish. Take out 1/2 the ambali in a cup. Now to the remaining ambali in the pot, add in 1.5 cups of Ragi flour, mix coarsely, close the lid and set on the lowest heat/flame. After 10 mins, open the lid, turn off the heat and mix away until well combined.  I couldn’t show this part in the photos because one hand and not a professional tiktoker 🤷‍♀️ In a separate bowl laced with ghee and keeping a small bowl of water on the side, you add a nice chunk of the ragi mudde into the ghee bowl, wet your hands with the water nearby, and take the mudde to make a ball using the ghee bowl. A little knead and ball action gets it smooth and round into the perfect little mudde. Store in an air tight container until ready to consume. #ragi #ragimudde #food #india #indianfood
